transcript.text:
A fridge-freezer not getting cold can be caused by simple things like a wrong temperature setting, blocked air vents inside, or a more complex issue with the cooling system itself. To narrow this down quickly: please check if the freezer compartment is still freezing hard (below -18°C) or if it is also warming up? Also, have you recently changed any settings on the control panel?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
freezer still freezing, about -17. havent changed any settings

Since the freezer is still cold, the cooling system itself is likely working, but the cold air isn't reaching the fridge section. The most common cause for this is airflow being restricted. Please check the vents inside the fridge compartment (usually on the back wall). Are they blocked by food containers or is the shelf packed so tightly that air cannot circulate freely? If you find blockages, move items aside to clear the path and see if it improves over a few hours.
moved the food away from the back, no difference. hardly any cold air from the slots

Since clearing the vents didn't help and there's hardly any air coming through, the cold isn't being moved from the freezer to the fridge. This usually means either the fan that pushes the air has stopped working, or ice has built up behind the panels blocking it. The quickest way to tell is to listen: with the door closed, can you hear a faint humming or whirring sound from inside the freezer? If it's silent, the fan motor may have failed; if there's noise but no cold air, ice might be jamming the blades.
motor running a lot. faint scraping/ticking from the freezer sometimes. no burning smell, nothing tripping

The 'motor running a lot' combined with that scraping/ticking sound suggests the fan blades are hitting a build-up of ice inside the freezer. This usually happens because the defrost system (which normally melts frost off the cooling coils) has failed, causing ice to grow until it jams the fan or blocks the air vents. To confirm this, please unplug the fridge-freezer and leave both doors open for 24 hours to let all hidden ice melt completely. After that time, plug it back in, close the doors, and tell me: does the faint scraping or ticking noise disappear once the appliance is running again?
did the 24h defrost with towels down. fridge got cold again within a day, 3C. not sure about the noise tho, couldnt tell

The fact that the fridge cooled down after your 24-hour manual defrost suggests that the cooling system works, but it also proves that ice has been building up inside and blocking the airflow again. This points strongly to a failure in the automatic defrost system (usually the heater or thermostat), which is why the ice returns. To confirm this, please unplug the fridge-freezer once more and remove the back panel inside the freezer compartment to expose the cooling coils. Is there a thick, solid block of ice covering those coils? If so, that suggests the defrost system has failed and needs repair.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
cant take the back panel off, no idea how and dont want to break the clips. its starting to creep up again after about 5 days tho

Since the fridge cooled down after your manual defrost but the problem returned within five days, this suggests that the automatic defrost system has failed. This is a common fault involving either the defrost heater or the thermostat/sensor that controls it. To help narrow down if there's an external cause contributing to this, please check two things: 1. Run your finger along the rubber door seal (gasket) all around, especially at the corners. Is it torn, loose, or sticky with food residue? 2. Look at the bottom of the freezer compartment for a small drain hole; is it clear and dry, or blocked by ice/debris?
seals look fine, doors close properly. not sure about the drain hole, cant tell

The pattern of cooling down after a manual defrost but icing up again within five days suggests that the automatic defrost system has failed. This is an internal fault involving parts like the defrost heater or thermostat that are not safe for you to replace without specialist tools and knowledge. Please contact a qualified appliance engineer to repair the defrost system, as this will resolve the recurring ice blockage.
